ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: keeps a lamp lit for travelers
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: visitors and caravans who stay the night leave on better terms (+1 goodwill a visit)

plain.li: I leave a lamp burning by the door at night now. Somebody out on the road might need to see it.
Since the guests went on their way, I trim the lamp in the window every evening before I go to bed.
[child] I put a candle in the window every night for people on the road. That's my job now.

warm.li: There are people out on the road tonight with nowhere to go. The least I can do is leave them a light.

blunt.li: Lamp stays lit at night. For whoever's out there.

cheerful.li: There's a lamp in our window every night now, and I'm the one who trims the wick!

gloomy.li: I keep a light burning for the ones still on the road. Most of them won't come this way.

cold.li: A light at night tells travelers the place is lived in and friendly. It costs a little oil.

plain.li: Forgot the lamp last night, and the night before. Maybe the road doesn't need it from me anymore.

warm.li: Someone else can keep the lamp now. I hope they do.

blunt.li: Stopped lighting the lamp. Oil's dear.

cheerful.li: I don't sit up with the lamp anymore, but I still wave at anyone coming up the road!

gloomy.li: The lamp's gone dark. If anyone came by its light, they never said.

cold.li: I have stopped lighting the lamp. Its effect on visitors was hard to measure.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: can't stand the smell of smoke

plain.li: Ever since the pyre, the smell of smoke turns my stomach. Even the cookfire.
I can't sit near the fire anymore. One breath of it and I'm back outside the gate that night.
[child] The big fire outside the gate smelled awful, and now every fire smells a bit like it.

warm.li: I know the fire keeps us warm. I just can't sit close to it since that night.

blunt.li: Can't stand smoke now. Not since the pyre.

cheerful.li: I'm sitting at the window end of the hall from now on. Fresh air, and plenty of it!

gloomy.li: The smoke from the pyre is still in my clothes. I've washed them twice. It must be in my head, then.

cold.li: Since the pyre, smoke unsettles me. The reaction is in the body, and I can't reason it away.

plain.li: Sat by the fire tonight and only smelled the wood. Good.

warm.li: I could sit at the fire with everyone again tonight. I've missed that.

cheerful.li: I toasted bread over the fire today and didn't think about anything but bread!

gloomy.li: The smell doesn't bother me anymore. I suppose I've forgotten that night. I'm not sure that's better.

cold.li: Smoke no longer affects me. The association has worn off.

plain.li: After that trader, I count the silver twice before anything changes hands. Then once more.
I keep a tally of every trade now, scratched on a scrap of hide in my pocket.

warm.li: I won't let anyone cheat us again. I count every coin for all of us now.

blunt.li: Got cheated once. Never again. I count everything.

cheerful.li: I can tell a short purse by the weight of it now! The traders don't like it one bit.

gloomy.li: Everyone out there wants to cheat us. So I count. Twice.

cold.li: Since I was cheated, I check every exchange. It is simply sensible.

plain.li: Paid a trader today without counting it twice. I think I trust my eyes again.

warm.li: I'll let someone else count the coins for a while. They'll do it fine.

cheerful.li: I've stopped counting the silver twice! Once is plenty when you're good at it.

gloomy.li: I've stopped counting twice. If they cheat us, they cheat us.

cold.li: I no longer count twice. The second count had stopped finding errors.

plain.li: I walk the fields every morning before breakfast now, turning leaves over, looking for anything that shouldn't be there.
After losing the crop, I check every row at first light. Found aphids on the corn today and pinched them off.

warm.li: I go out to the fields at dawn. If something's wrong I'd rather find it early, before it costs us a winter.

blunt.li: Fields at dawn. Every day. Not losing another crop.

cheerful.li: I'm out in the fields before the sun every morning! The dew soaks my boots, but the beans look grand.

gloomy.li: We lost a crop once. I walk the rows every morning, waiting for it to happen again.

cold.li: Early inspection catches pests before they spread. I walk the fields at dawn.

plain.li: Slept through dawn today, and the fields were fine without me.

warm.li: The fields are healthy. I've let the morning walks go, mostly.

blunt.li: Stopped the dawn walks. Fields are fine.

cheerful.li: I've stopped walking the rows at dawn! The plants seem to manage.

gloomy.li: I don't check the fields at dawn anymore. Whatever comes will come.

cold.li: The daily inspection has ended. Losses have been low.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: keeps a dream book
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: dreams more often, and writes every dream down

plain.li: A dream of mine came true, so now I keep a book by the bed and write each dream down before it goes.
I wake, reach for the charcoal, and write. Most of it makes no sense by breakfast.
[child] I have a book for my dreams now. I draw the ones I can't spell.

warm.li: I write my dreams down every morning now. If one of them is a warning, I want to be able to tell everyone.

blunt.li: Dreams go in the book. In case.

cheerful.li: I've got a dream book! Last night's had a goat in a hat in it, so I drew the hat.

gloomy.li: One dream came true. Now I write them all down and wait to see which is next.

cold.li: One dream proved accurate. I now record them all, to see whether it happens again.

plain.li: Haven't written in the dream book for a week. The dreams have gone back to being dreams.

warm.li: I've put the dream book away. If I ever need it again, it's in the chest by my bed.

blunt.li: Done with the dream book. Just dreams.

cheerful.li: I've filled the dream book, and I'm not starting another. Too many goats.

gloomy.li: None of the others came true. I stopped writing them down.

cold.li: The dream record yielded nothing further. I've stopped keeping it.

plain.li: The healer left me a pot of salve and told me what goes in it. I rub it into every cut now, and they close quicker, I swear.
I make the healer's salve myself now: tallow, a few leaves from the field edge, and a lot of stirring.

warm.li: That healer was kind to me. I keep the salve they showed me, and I share it with anyone who's hurt.

blunt.li: Got the healer's salve. It works. I use it.

cheerful.li: Scraped knee? Salve. Sore hands? Salve! I've grown very fond of this salve.

gloomy.li: The healer's salve is the only thing I trust when I'm hurt. Everything else wears off.

cold.li: The healer's ointment speeds healing. I can't say exactly why. I use it anyway.

plain.li: The last of the salve ran out and I didn't make more.

warm.li: I gave the last jar of salve to someone who needed it more.

cheerful.li: Haven't needed the salve in ages! I'm in very good repair.

gloomy.li: The salve's gone. Cuts heal the slow way again.

cold.li: I no longer use the salve. The supply ran out.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: juggles at supper
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: juggles for those eating or resting nearby (a little recreation for each of them)

plain.li: After the players left I tried juggling three potatoes. Now I can do it, and I do it at supper whether anyone asks or not.
I practiced with stones behind the barn until I stopped dropping them. Now it's spoons at the table.
[child] I can juggle three things now. Four if one of them is a sock.

warm.li: I learned to juggle so the others would have something to smile at over supper. It works most nights.

blunt.li: I juggle now. At supper. Watch or don't.

cheerful.li: I can juggle! Spoons, apples, a boot once. Supper is a show now.

gloomy.li: I juggle at supper. It gives everyone something to look at besides the empty chairs.

cold.li: I practiced juggling until I could do it without thinking. It keeps the hands busy at meals.

plain.li: Dropped all three apples at supper tonight, and didn't pick them back up to try again.

warm.li: I've put the spoons down. The children do the juggling now anyway.

cheerful.li: My juggling days are over! I went out on a good catch.

gloomy.li: I stopped juggling. The others had stopped watching first.

cold.li: I have stopped juggling at meals. The novelty wore off.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: swears by a trick against the cold

plain.li: A traveler showed me how they keep the frost off: dry wraps next to the skin, grease on the face, never sweat outside. I do it all now.
I wrap my feet the traveler's way now, with dry grass between the layers. My toes haven't been cold since.

warm.li: That traveler's trick for the cold works. I've shown it to anyone who'll stand still long enough.

blunt.li: Grease on the face, dry feet, don't sweat. Cold doesn't bother me now.

cheerful.li: I've got a trick for the cold now! I look ridiculous with my face greased, but I'm warm.

gloomy.li: The cold still comes. I've just learned to keep it at the door a while longer.

cold.li: A traveler taught me a method against the cold. It works. I use it.

plain.li: I've stopped bothering with the traveler's trick. I've got used to the cold the ordinary way.

warm.li: I hope that traveler's somewhere warm tonight. I've forgotten half their trick.

blunt.li: Forgot the cold trick. Wear a coat.

cheerful.li: I've given up greasing my face! The others are relieved.

gloomy.li: The trick stopped working, or I stopped doing it right.

cold.li: I no longer follow the traveler's method. Ordinary clothing does well enough.
